rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation for the participial wording rather than the verb is its relation to what precedes.
rows.anchor: دون يخرجون فقيل ما سبق وقيل استوى هنا يخرجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the participle and verb as equal in meaning; the noun is chosen for its lightness and lexical rootedness.
rows.anchor: وقيل استوى هنا يخرجون وخارجين في إفادة المعنى واختير الاسم لخفته واصالته

words: قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they return to their satans, they report their own steadfast allegiance to them.
rows.anchor: يخبرون عن انفسهم بالثبات على الايمان بهم

words: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي
rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the stronger concern with bringing the living from the dead calls for the imperfect, which signals renewal, as in God's mockery of them.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي لأن الاعتناء بشأن إخراج الحي من الميت لما كان أشد أتى بالمضارع ليدل على التجدد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority holds that metaphor occurs in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على الوقوع وأنكره جماعه منهم ابن القاص من الشافعية

rows.speaker: ابن القاص وابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qass, Ibn Khuwayz Mindad, and others deny Qur'anic metaphor: a speaker turns to metaphor only when literal expression is constrained, which they deem impossible for God.
rows.anchor: وأنكره جماعه منهم ابن القاص من الشافعية وابن خويز منداد من المالكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection fails: excluding metaphor would also exclude emphasis, ellipsis, repeated narratives, and much of the Qur'an's beauty.
rows.anchor: ولو وجب خلو القرآن من المجاز لوجب خلوه من التوكيد والحذف وتثنية القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Muhammad Ibn Abd al-Salam composed a separate work on metaphor and covered the subject comprehensively.
rows.anchor: وقد افرده بالصنيف الإمام أبو محمد بن عبد السلام وجمع فأوعى

rows.speaker: الحاتمي
rows.claim: Al-Hatimi derives majaz as a verbal noun meaning the path or source of speech, by analogy with maqam from qumtu.
rows.anchor: قال الحاتمي معناه طريق القول ومأخذه مصدر جزت مجازا كما يقال قمت مقاما

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i characterizes Arabic speech as formed through examples and likenesses.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي كلام العرب إنما هو مثال شبه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Metaphor has two causes: resemblance, called lexical metaphor and discussed by legal theorists, and association, called rational metaphor and discussed by linguists.
rows.anchor: أحدهما الشبه ويسمى المجاز اللغوي وهو الذي يتكلم فيه الأصولي والثاني الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational metaphor is attributing a word to something other than its proper subject through an interpretive relation, such as crediting a cause with an act.
rows.anchor: وهو ان تسند الكلمة إلى غير ماهي له اصالة بضرب من التأويل كسب زيد اباه اذا كان سببا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase of faith is attributed to the recited verses, and ruin to a person's supposition, because each is a cause of the result.
rows.anchor: ونسبت الزيادة التي هي فعل الله إلى الآيات لكونها سببا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slaughter is ascribed to Pharaoh as the one ordering it, while stripping is ascribed to Satan because his temptation caused the couple to eat.
rows.anchor: والفاعل غيره ونسب الفعل اليه لكونه الآمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes the trade itself the grammatical subject of profit, an example of rational metaphor.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ فما ربحت تجارتهم ﴾ جعل التجارة الرابحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “when the matter is resolved,” the matter is what is resolved upon; the wording is clarified by the command to resolve and then rely on God.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فإذا عزم الأمر ﴾ لآن الأمر هو المعزوم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders are credited with bringing their people to ruin because their commands caused the people's disbelief.
rows.anchor: فنسب الإحلال الذي هو فعل الله إلى اكابرهم لان سببه كفرهم وسبب كفرهم امر اكابرهم اياهم بالكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle ma can precede nouns and verbs; with a noun it can work like laysa, raising the subject and putting the predicate in the accusative in Hijazi usage.
rows.anchor: ففي الأسماء ك ليس ترفع وتنصب في لغة اهل الحجاز ووقع في القرآن في ثلاث مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a past verb, ma has no grammatical effect and means lam, as in the verse's denial that their trade profited.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأفعال فلا تعمل وتدخل على الماضي بمعنى لم نحو ما خرج أي لم يخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before an imperfect verb, ma negates the present, like la, denying that the act is occurring now.
rows.anchor: وعلى المضارع لنفي الحال بمعنى لا نحو ما يخرج زيد اي لا يخرج نفيت أن يكون منه خروج في الحال

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says ma negates the present in both Hijazi and Tamimi usage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب هي لنفي الحال في اللغتين الحجازية والتميمية نحو ما زيد منطلقا ومنطلق

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib allows ma to negate past or future when contextual clues establish that sense.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب هي لنفي الحال في اللغتين الحجازية والتميمية نحو ما زيد منطلقا ومنطلق ولهذا جعلها سيبويه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats ma as an emphatic negative, parallel to qad in affirmative speech, since qad itself conveys emphasis and proximity to the present.
rows.anchor: جعلها سيبويه في النفي جوابا لقد في الإثبات ولا ريب إن قد للتقريب من الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma can negate a completed past, as in the unbelievers' claim that no bearer of good news or warning came; the context explains it as their future excuse after proof.
rows.anchor: فإنه ورد للتعليل على معنى كراهة إن يقولوا عند إقامة الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives a Qur'anic counting rule: ma followed by illa is negative in thirteen places, beginning with three examples listed from al-Baqara and al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: وهنا ضابط وهو إذا ما اتت بعدها إلا في القرآن فهي من نفي إلا في ثلاثة عشر موضعا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some call the negative particle jaḥd, while others reject that label; the author notes that the distinction between jaḥd and negation was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يسميه جحدا وأنكره بعضهم وسبق الفرق بين الجحد والنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif and lam occur frequently in Qur'anic openings because they are common letters in speech.
rows.anchor: فلأن الألف واللام كثرت فى الفواتح دون غيرها من الحروف لكثرتها فى الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters also carry articulatory significance: hamza is deepest, lam is made at the tongue tip against the upper palate, and mim at the closed lips.
rows.anchor: أن الهمزة من الرئة فهى أعمق الحروف واللام مخرجها من طرف اللسان ملصقة بصدر الغار الأعلى من الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those letters can stand for the rest, just as the testimony of faith entails its other requirements, alluded to in the Prophet's command to fight until people affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: ويرمز بهن إلى باقى الحروف كما رمز صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of ta with sin and ha is meaningful: ta gathers five articulatory qualities, while sin is its contrasting unvoiced, soft, sibilant counterpart.
rows.anchor: فإن الطاء جمعت من صفات الحروف خمس صفات لم يجمعها غيرها وهى الجهر والشدة والاستعلاء والإطباق والإصمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah Qaf is built around qaf-sounding words and themes, repeatedly returning to the Qur'an, creation, speech, the recording angels, judgment, and provision.
rows.anchor: فإن السورة مبنية على الكلمات القافية من ذكر القرآن ومن ذكر الخلق وتكرار القول ومراجعته مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's meanings also suit qaf's forceful, voiced, emphatic, vibrating, open articulation.
rows.anchor: وسر آخر وهو أن كل معانى السورة مناسب لما فى حرف القاف من الشدة والجهر والقلقلة والانفتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah Sad's repeated disputes form a structural pattern: unbelievers challenge the Prophet, litigants confront David, the people of Hell and the heavenly assembly dispute, and Iblis argues against God's command and vows to mislead humanity.
rows.anchor: فتأمل ما اشتملت عليه سورة ص من الخصومات المتعددة فاولها خصومة الكفار مع النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mushaf copies vary in the spellings of Harut, Marut, Haman, and Qarun; Dawud keeps its alif because a waw is already omitted, and most copies similarly retain alif in Isra'il after deleting ya.
rows.anchor: واختلفت المصاحف فى أربعة هاروت وماروت وهامان وقارون فأما داود فلا خلاف فى رسمه بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound masculine and feminine plurals are generally written without alif; the alif remains when a hamza or doubled letter follows it.
rows.anchor: وكذلك اتفقوا على حذف الألف فى جمع السلامة مذكرا كان كالعلمين والصبرين والصدقين أو مؤنثا

rows.speaker: ابو العباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas explains spelling by whether a quality is viewed from a lower, visible, worldly aspect, which favors retaining alif, or a higher, spiritual aspect, which favors deletion.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العباس وقد تكون الصفة ملكوتية روحانية وتعتبر من جهة مرتبة سفلى ملكية هى أظهر فى الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some orthographic contrasts are transparent, as in the differing treatment of al-akhīr and al-ashrār; other spellings require subtler reflection.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما يكون ظاهر الفرقان كالأخير والأشرار تحذف من الأول دون الثانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-firash and al-ta'am, despite similar weight and physical referents, the first is considered through its tangible simile while the second is the tangible food given to the needy.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما يخفى كالفراش ويطعمون الطعام فالفراش محسوس والطعام ثابت ووزنهما واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the paired food verse, alif is retained for the People of the Book's food as relatively lower, but omitted for the believers' food as relatively higher because of Islam's superiority.
rows.anchor: ثبتت الألف فى الأول لأنه سفلى بالنسبة إلى طعامنا لمكان التشديد عليهم فيه وحذفت من الثانى لأنه علوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is omitted in “they both ate food” because this food is viewed as higher.
rows.anchor: لعلو هذا الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled form “the doors were shut” conveys intensive action and includes spiritual doors of reliance, so its alif is omitted; singular physical door references distinguish the concrete door.
rows.anchor: ليس بمحسوس من أبواب الاعتصام فحذفت الألف لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is omitted from “when they came out against Goliath” because the episode is viewed as spiritual and elevated; the alif is kept in the account of David killing the embodied Goliath.
rows.anchor: حذف لأنه الاسم ﴿ وقتل داود جالوت ﴾ ثبت لأنه مجسد محسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in “its gates were opened” is omitted because the opened gates are spiritual and elevated; it is retained in “the gates are opened for them” and in the count of seven gates as concrete worldly forms.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وفتحت أبوابها ﴾ محذوف لأنها من حيث فتحت ملكوتية علوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif is retained in locusts as a tangible single specimen but omitted in frogs, whose plural is treated as a spiritual sign rather than a single tangible instance.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الجراد والضفدع الأول ثابت فهو الذى فى الواحدة المحسوسة والثانى محذوف لأنه ليس فى الواحدة المحسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spelling of amthal changes with specificity: alif is omitted for unspecified universal likenesses and retained when the comparison is specified, such as pearl whiteness and purity; detailed tangible examples differ from implicit ones.
rows.anchor: حذفت لأنها أمثال كلية لم يتعين فيها للفهم جهة التماثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated forms for the trumpet blast and the earth's crushing differ because the first is spiritual and known through faith, while the second is physical and imaginable.
rows.anchor: الأولى محذوفة لأنها روحانية لا تعلم إلا إيمانا والثانية ثابتة جسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in “my book” is omitted as spiritual, while that in “my account” is retained as worldly, although both refer to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: محذوفة لأنه ملكوتى وألف ﴿ حسابيه ﴾ ثابتة لأنها ملكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual case is written without alif, while the tangible worldly possession retains it.
rows.anchor: ملكوتية / وماليه / ملكى محسوس فحذف الأول وثبت الثانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For subhan, alif is omitted as spiritual except in one disputed place; the author prefers omission there too, since the Prophet's elevated presence is not distracted by worldly movement.
rows.anchor: ومن أسقط فلعلو حال المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يشغله عن الحضور تقلبه فى الملكوت الخطاب فى الملك وهو أولى الوجهين

words: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the demand for a single revelation by explaining that gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet's heart; new revelation at each event renews care, reassurance, and his connection with the angel and message.
rows.anchor: أى لنقوى به قلبك فإن الوحى إذا كان يتجدد فى كل حادثة كان أقوى للقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated arrival of Gabriel brought the Prophet joy, and the text connects this to his exceptional generosity in Ramadan, when Gabriel came more often.
rows.anchor: وتجديد العهد به وبما معه من الرسالة الواردة من ذلك الجانب العزيز فحدث له من السرور ما تقصر عنه العبارة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that gradual revelation helped the unlettered Prophet memorize the Qur'an, unlike literate prophets who could retain a complete revelation at once.
rows.anchor: لنحفظه فإنه عليه السلام كان اميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب ففرق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God could have enabled the Prophet to memorize the whole Qur'an at once, not every possible event has to occur; questions and the need for abrogation also account for piecemeal revelation.
rows.anchor: قلت ليس كل ممكن لازم الوقوع وأيضا فى القرآن أجوبة عن أسئلة فهو سبب من أسباب تفرق النزول ولأن بعضه منسوخ وبعضه ناسخ

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Furak reports that the Torah came down at once to literate Moses, whereas the unwritten Qur'an came gradually to an unlettered Prophet; he also cites abrogation, answers to questions, and timely denials.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فورك قيل أنزلت التوراة جملة لأنها نزلت على نبى يقرأ ويكتب وهو موسى وأنزل القرآن مفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interval from the first to last revelation is given as twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years, depending on whether the Prophet lived in Mecca after the call for ten, thirteen, or fifteen years; his Medina period was ten years.
rows.anchor: وكان بين أول نزول القرآن آخره عشرون أو ثلاث وعشرون أو خمس وعشرون سنة وهو مبنى على الخلاف فى مدة إقامته صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever revelation came, the Prophet ordered it written and specified the surah where separate verses belonged.
rows.anchor: وكان كلما أنزل عليه شىء من القرآن أمر بكتابته ويقول فى مفترقات الآيات ضعوا هذه فى سورة كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel reviewed the Qur'an with the Prophet once each Ramadan and twice in the year he died.
rows.anchor: وكان يعرضه جبريل فى شهر رمضان كل عام مرة وعام مات مرتين

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says the conditional particle in conveys frequency through its broad, indefinite scope; its use with ahad, normally restricted to general negation, illustrates this.
rows.anchor: ادعى ابن جني في كتاب القد إن إن الشرطية تفيد معنى التكثير لما كان في هذا الشياع والعموم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni allows ahad here to mean one individual rather than the generalizing negative pronoun; the conditional in supplies the generality, as in “if a woman” and “if a man.”
rows.anchor: قال يجوز إن تكون أحد هنا ليست التي للعموم بل بمنزلة أحد من احد وعشرين ونحوه إلا انه دخله معنى العموم لاجل إن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the condition is inherent in the prohibition: if the women do not seek chastity, they seek prostitution, and coercing them into what they seek makes no sense.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال اما الاولى فيمتنع النهي عن ارادة التحصن فانهن اذا لم يردن التحصن يردن البغاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other readings take in as “when,” or as an inserted condition: the ban is emphatic because owners would coerce women precisely when they wanted chastity.
rows.anchor: وقيل انها بمعنى اذا لانه لايجوز اكراههن على الزنا إن لم يردن التحصن أو هو شرط مقحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth example seems to presuppose that the full prayer is the original form, but the author rejects that assumption, citing Aisha: prayer began as two cycles, remained so in travel, and was increased for residents.
rows.anchor: واما الرابعة فهو يشعر بالاتمام ولا نسلم إن الاصل الاتمام وقد قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها فرضت الصلاة ركعتين

words: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the remaining examples, the apparent conditional sense is contextually implausible, but an incidental factor can still license departure from the surface reading.
rows.anchor: واما البواقي فظاهر الشرط ممتنع فيه بدليل التعجب المذكور لكنه لا يمنع مخالفة الظاهر لعارض

words: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travel-and-collateral clause is among the Qur'anic conditional constructions whose condition is discussed as not necessarily intended literally.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate open-hamza particle an is a verbal-noun particle governing a subjunctive imperfect; its clause can serve as subject, agent, object, or genitive complement.
rows.anchor: حرفا مصدريا ناصبا للفعل المضارع وتقع معه في موقع المبتدأ والفاعل والمفعول والمضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written feminine ending has two aspects: as a name or quality its ta is closed; when it signifies an act or visible effect, it is extended.
rows.anchor: أحدهما من حيث هى أسماء وصفات وهذا تقبض منه التاء والثانى من حيث أن يكون مقتضاها فعلا وأثرا ظاهرا فى الوجود فهذا تمد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahmah is written with extended ta in seven places; “near” is masculine in one example, marking the active sense, and the mention of traces likewise signals an effect.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك الرحمة مدت فى سبعة مواضع للعلة المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ni'mah is usually written with closed ta, but eleven places extend it; in Ibrahim the human-centered ending “the human is unjust, ungrateful” marks an actual worldly favor.
rows.anchor: أن الحاصلة بالفعل فى الوجود تمد نحو قوله فى إبراهيم

words: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel Nahl wording has closed ta because the favor is framed as coming from God and ends with God's forgiveness and mercy, a spiritual aspect.
rows.anchor: كتبت مقبوضة لأنها بمعنى الاسم بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalimah is written with closed ta except in this A'raf instance, where its completion has a manifest effect in worldly existence and is therefore extended.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الكلمة مقبوضة إلا فى موضع فى الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunnah is written with closed ta except in five places where it means destruction and retribution occurring in existence.
rows.anchor: ومنها السنة مقبوضة إلا فى خمسة مواضع حيث تكون بمعنى الإهلاك والانتقام الذى فى الوجود

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats uluwwan in “exalted with great exaltation” as a verbal noun in place of ta'aliyan; al-Raghib agrees, while allowing that it can be a verbal noun elsewhere too.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء هو موضع تعاليا لانه مصدر قوله ﴿ وتعالى ﴾ ويجوز ان يقع مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording avoids the tafa''ul form because it can suggest effort or affectation, as it does with human speakers.
rows.anchor: وانما عدل عنه لان لفظ التفاعل من التكلف كما يكون من البشر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow metaphor in either component of “the sky heaves a heaving and the mountains move”: the sky may only seem to heave, or its inhabitants may undergo the genuine motion; the same alternatives apply to mountains.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم الجملة الفاعلية تحتمل المجاز في مفرديها جميعا وفي كل منهما مثاله ها هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer treats the cognate nouns as implicit repetitions of their verbs, so each clause emphasizes the same action twice and the ambiguity disappears.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بهذه القاعدة وهي ان ﴿ مورا ﴾ في تقدير تمور فكانه قال تمور السماء تمور السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the exception, shay'an may be an emphatic cognate object, or it may mean an affair or clarification placed where a verbal noun would stand; this also challenges the claim that a general object of will must be omitted.
rows.anchor: واما قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا ﴾ فيحتمل ان يكون ﴿ شيئا ﴾ من تأكيد الفعل بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated dakkan means successive crushing, one after another; saffan likewise means row following row, since a single form could suggest only one row.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به التتابع أي دكا بعد دك وكذا قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive in “its own quake” signals the earth's distinctive, familiar, expected earthquake, like a person's characteristic anger or fighting; the poet's repeated phrase illustrates this emphasis.
rows.anchor: فان اضافة الزلزال اليها يفيد معنى ذاتها وهو زلزالها المختص بها المعروف منها المتوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart can stand for intellect, mouths for tongues, tongue for language, and a village for its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالقلب عن الفعل كقوله ﴿ لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ﴾ اي عقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A state may be named for its place: being in God's mercy means being in Paradise, plotting of night and day means plotting during them, and security or goodness predicated of a town describes its inhabitants or air.
rows.anchor: إطلاق اسم الحال على المحل كقوله تعالى ﴿ وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون ﴾

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “in your sleep” as “in your eye”; al-Zamakhshari regards that as remote and construes it as “in your vision.”
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن في قوله ﴿ إذ يريكهم الله في منامك ﴾ اي في عينك واستبعده الزمخشري وقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “take your adornment at every mosque,” adornment means its place, while mosque means prayer; the former is an abstract state and the latter its place.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمع هذا والذي قبله في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An instrument can name its effect: “a tongue of truth” means good remembrance, eyes mean God's sight, and a messenger's tongue means his people's language.
rows.anchor: الثامن عشر إطلاق اسم آلة الشيء عليه كقوله تعالى ﴿ واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word can be transferred to its opposite: requital for an evil deed is called evil from the wrongdoer's perspective, though it is good from God; likewise obedience is called ihsan in a phrase about its reward.
rows.anchor: التاسع عشر إطلاق اسم الضدين على الاخر كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fight them; God will punish them by your hands” raises the problem of how the believers act while God is the true punisher, and why they are commanded if God acts by moving their hands; resolving it requires understanding human capacity and divine power.
rows.anchor: فإذا كانوا هم القاتلين كيف يكون الله تعالى هو المعذب وإن كان تعالى هو المعذب بتحريك ايديهم فما معنى امرهم بالقتال

words: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic explanation transmitted by al-Bukhari identifies the “wrong” that believers must not mix with faith as associationism.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك تفسير الظلم بالشرك في قوله تعالى ﴿ الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's Prophetic explanation glosses the easy reckoning as presentation.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الحساب اليسير بالعرض رواهما البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report in Muslim explains the commanded “strength” as archery, which the author says refutes Mujahid's interpretation as cavalry.
rows.anchor: وتفسير القوة في ﴿ وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ﴾ بالرمي رواه مسلم وبذلك يرد تفسير مجاهد بالخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also gives a Prophetic gloss of worship as supplication.
rows.anchor: وكتفسير العبادة بالدعاء في قوله ﴿ إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي ﴾

rows.speaker: الميموني عن أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Al-Maimuni quotes Ahmad as saying that the books of campaigns, apocalyptic battles, and Qur'anic commentary lack foundations; Ahmad's careful interpreters mean that most reports in them lack sound connected chains, though many sound reports exist.
rows.anchor: قال الميموني سمعت أحمد بن حنبل يقول ثلاث كتب ليس لها اصول المغازي والملاحم والتفسير

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim treats a Companion's interpretation as equivalent to a report raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فإن تفسيره عندهم بمنزلة المرفوع إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما قاله الحاكم في تفسيره

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abu al-Khattab says a Companion's statement might not bind if it is not proof; the author prefers treating it as proof because tafsir is transmitted report, not personal opinion.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الخطاب من الحنابلة يحتمل الا يرجع اليه اذا قلنا ان قوله ليس بحجة والصواب الأول

rows.speaker: مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud swears that he knew the person and place of revelation for every verse, and would travel to anyone who knew the Qur'an better; he also says learners did not move beyond ten verses before learning their meaning and practice.
rows.anchor: ابن جرير عن مسروق وقال عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening of al-Hajj was revealed at night during the Banu al-Mustaliq expedition while the people were traveling.
rows.anchor: نزلت ليلا فى غزوة بن المصطلق وهم حى من خزاعة والناس يسيرون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة
rows.claim: Ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah reports that this verse came during an expedition after Hudhayfa, Sa'd, and others guarded the Prophet's leather tent overnight; the Prophet then announced that God had protected him.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من يحرسنا الليلة فأتاه حذيفة وسعد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says this verse was revealed while she and the Prophet were sharing a blanket.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها نزلت هذه الآية على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا معه فى اللحاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the Qur'an was revealed during the daytime.
rows.anchor: ونزل عليه أكثر القرآن نهارا

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
rows.claim: A report says al-An'am descended all at once with seventy thousand angels filling the space between heaven and earth, praising God, after which the Prophet praised God and prostrated.
rows.anchor: سورة الأنعام نزلت مرة واحدة شيعها سبعون ألف ملك طبقوا ما بين السموات والأرض لهم زجل بالتسبيح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن الصلاح
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Salah says the report of al-An'am descending all at once through Ubayy ibn Ka'b has a weak chain and no sound chain was found; contrary reports say some of it came down in Medina, with disagreement whether three, six, or another number of verses.
rows.anchor: ذكر أبو عمرو بن الصلاح فى فتاويه أن الخبر المذكور جاء من حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports say al-Fatiha descended with eighty thousand angels, the Throne Verse and Yunus with thirty thousand each, and “Ask those We sent before you” with twenty thousand.
rows.anchor: وفاتحة الكتاب نزلت ومعها ثمانون ألف ملك وآية الكرسي نزلت ومعها ثلاثون ألف ملك وسورة يونس نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the Qur'an descended with Gabriel without an angelic escort.
rows.anchor: وسائر القرآن نزل به جبريل بلا تشييع
